title: A steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based BCI dataset in children and adolescents
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 47 neurotypical children and adolescents (ages 5-18) who completed a two-stage steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) brain-computer interface (BCI) session, including a stimulus personalization pipeline and an online 4-target SSVEP game. Data were collected as part of the BCI4Kids program to support development of signal-processing methods for pediatric SSVEP-BCI applications. The dataset was converted from raw XDF recordings into BIDS-compliant BrainVision format using mne-bids.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a g.tec g.GAMMAsys gel-based system (g.USBamp, g.GAMMAcap) with 16 channels at 256 Hz, earlobe reference, and Fpz ground. Participants completed a stimulus personalization task (12 stimuli, 4 contrasts x 3 sizes, flickering at 10 Hz) followed by an online 4-target SSVEP game (6.25/10/11.11/14.28 Hz) played on two themed maps. Raw XDF recordings were converted to BrainVision format with mne-bids, deriving channels.tsv, events.tsv, and JSON sidecars, following channel order, scaling, and standard_1020 montage conventions from the MOABB Schrag2026Pediatric reader.
